clue.text: As cruel, unfortunately, as some layman

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain ordinary person is as cruel as anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the seven letters of AS CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is not clergy, and secular describes worldly, non-religious life.

clue.text: An essential boost for South Africa's fruit

parts.note: SA is the standard abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue a boost lifts the piece upwards, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: an essential is a must, so the phrase gives A MUST

explanation.surface: Something vital that gives South Africa's fruit industry a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boost' lifts A MUST in this down clue, giving TSUMA; South Africa comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned citrus, a type of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Shock — initially calming legislation unleashes mass panic!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A soothing new law that backfires and sets off widespread alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick bunch or tuft of it.

clue.text: Pig cause of daughter overturning car in country road

indicators.note: in places the daughter-and-car piece inside the word for a country road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning flips the word upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A pig blamed for a daughter's car crash on a rural road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' flips CAR to RAC; 'cause of' is padding, and 'Pig' is a breed name.
explanation.definitionFit: Landrace is a breed of long white domestic pig.

clue.text: Beams to lift, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to lift something is to raise it

explanation.surface: Beams of a building being hoisted into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow lines of light, as beams are.

clue.text: Torrid zone where king is mobbed by subjects

indicators.note: being mobbed means surrounded by a crowd, so the king goes inside the other word

parts.note: subjects of discussion are topics
R, from Latin rex, is the standard abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A hot region where a monarch is swamped by his own people.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot belt either side of the equator, once called the torrid zone.

clue.text: Liquid poured out from pint tureen

indicators.note: pouring out spills the contents into a new arrangement, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Soup being ladled out of a serving dish into a pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poured out' rearranges the letters of PINT TUREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a volatile oil used as a paint solvent.

clue.text: Gear seizure beyond the exit

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the seizure follows the exit

parts.note: the way out, the exit, gives OUT
a seizure is a fit

explanation.surface: Equipment confiscated just past the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes or kit, as gear is.

clue.text: I'm inept at jumping, being short

indicators.note: jumping letters leap about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone admits being clumsy at jumping because of their small stature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges INEPT AT into PATIENT after I'M; 'short' means short-tempered, not small.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone means being curt and lacking patience.

clue.text: Leathery joints of meat?

parts.note: reads like tough cuts of meat, but means the leather seats of horse riders, which share their name with a butcher's cut of lamb or venison

explanation.surface: A complaint about tough, chewy cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is both a leather riding seat and a joint cut from an animal's back.

clue.text: Enter your knock-out of this knight in the lists

indicators.note: a knock-out scatters things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up a knight for a jousting knock-out competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock-out' rearranges ENTER YOUR. The lists are the arena for jousting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourneyer is one who fights in a tourney, a medieval jousting tournament.

clue.text: Times leader copied for the video?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to copy is to ape someone

explanation.surface: A Times editorial plagiarised for a video.
explanation.definitionFit: Taped means recorded, as a programme put on video is.

clue.text: Judge large bird is about to tear back

indicators.note: back sends the whole assembled piece backwards
being about something means surrounding it, so the bird goes round the tear

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
to tear is to rip

explanation.surface: A big bird preparing to dash back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' wraps the bird round the tear, giving ERIPMU, and 'back' reverses the whole. 'tear' is the verb, not crying.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire adjudicates a game, acting as its judge.

clue.text: By fiddling, trim late payment

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cooking the books to cut a late payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By fiddling' rearranges TRIM LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittal is a remittance, money sent to settle a bill.

clue.text: Dejected, no strong drink being to hand?

definitions.text: no strong drink being to hand?
definitions.meaning: humorously, without any spirits such as whisky or gin in the house

explanation.surface: Feeling down because there is no hard liquor in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking vigour describes a downcast person, and jokingly a home lacking any whisky or gin.

clue.text: Prepare for programme I can tape it!

indicators.note: to programme is to arrange, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready for a TV show by recording it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' looks like a TV show but is a verb rearranging I CAN TAPE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to foresee it and make ready ahead of time.

clue.text: Sick duck on river seeking fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue being on something means sitting below it, so these follow the river

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England
sick means ill
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: An ailing duck on a river searching for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarillo is a red egg-shaped tropical fruit, also called the tree tomato.

clue.text: Pass the port back, by god!

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Suez is the Egyptian port at the southern end of the canal

explanation.surface: A dinner-table call to send the port round, with an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass the port' is the after-dinner custom of passing a decanter; 'Pass' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the king of the Greek deities.

clue.text: Ships in Gateshead gone tomorrow

parts.note: a fleet is a body of ships
the head of the word gate is its first letter G

explanation.surface: Vessels that call in at Gateshead, a town on the Tyne in north-east England, and leave the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone tomorrow' recalls 'here today, gone tomorrow' for something brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting is transient, here today and soon vanished.

clue.text: Police post to which a gang retreated

indicators.note: retreated means went backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a mob is a gang

explanation.surface: A gang falling back to the safety of a police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' reverses A MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa a boma is a stockade, also used for a police outpost.

clue.text: Hear nasty virus around — restriction on movement called for

indicators.note: the virus word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus

indicators.note: nasty suggests something unpleasant done to the word, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Hearing of a nasty bug going round, so lockdown is demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' jumbles HEAR to EARH; 'around' signals the virus word enclosing it. The surface evokes lockdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight clinch pins someone's arms, restricting their movement.

clue.text: Spelled out how, with delays on the railway, I missed out on first date

indicators.note: missed out means the named letter is dropped

parts.words: how, with delays on the railway
parts.note: a delayed railway service is described as trains late

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A frustrated commuter explaining how delayed trains made them miss a first date.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAINS LATE loses its I through 'missed out', then D, the first letter of 'date', is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Translated means rendered into another language, i.e. explained in plain words.

clue.text: Flower parasite most difficult to fathom

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee
a pest is a parasite or nuisance

explanation.surface: A plant parasite that is a real mystery to identify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, here the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest means most profound, so hardest to understand.

clue.text: Has a good time being taken around then taken aback

indicators.note: being taken around shifts the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Enjoying a guided tour and then being startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken around' rearranges HAS A G into AGHAS before T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes someone shocked and startled.

clue.text: Appropriate for English spa town to lose hospital

indicators.note: to lose means the named letter is removed

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Whether it is fitting for a Yorkshire resort to lose its hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the verb, to seize, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize for oneself without right.

clue.text: Insect let free by another

parts.note: a bee is another insect

indicators.note: set free, the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A bug released by a second bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' scrambles LET to TLE; 'another' means another insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases.

clue.text: Only half 'crown? It surely cost more than that!

definitions.text: Only half 'crown? It surely cost more than that!

parts.words: Only half 'crown? It surely cost more than that!
parts.note: suggests the old half-crown coin as a price, but describes a jewelled headpiece that is less than a full crown and far dearer

explanation.surface: Scoffing at someone claiming a purchase cost only half a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-crown was an old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled semicircular headband, a partial coronet.

clue.text: Question an inflammatory device

definitions.meaning: to quiz someone persistently for information
jokingly, a gadget that blows things up, as when inflating a tyre

explanation.surface: Interrogating someone about an incendiary bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump a person is to quiz them; a pump also inflates tyres and balloons.

clue.text: Game small boy leads mother

indicators.note: leads means comes first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry, a boy's name
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A little lad guiding his mum by the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across a chequered board.

clue.text: Clarify cryptic clue one meets at specific time of year

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are obscured by rearrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a date is a specific day of the year

explanation.surface: Solving a cryptic clue by meeting someone on a set day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUE into ELUC.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make clear or explain.

clue.text: The speaker's assistant? Log off — time to sit back!

indicators.note: off means spoilt or gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
back reverses the letters of the word

explanation.surface: An aide to the Commons Speaker logging off for a sit-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles LOG to GLO and 'back' turns SIT to TIS. The Speaker chairs Britain's House of Commons, but here a speaker is anyone talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the vocal opening in the larynx, so it helps anyone who talks.

clue.text: Show insect sitting on leaf

indicators.note: sitting on means the insect comes after the leaf here

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug resting on a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public spectacle or procession.
